Provide the shared persistence model and user-aware data access foundation used across the platform.

What it owns

  • Owns CoreDataContext and the platform entity model.
  • Applies app, tenant and user-aware query behaviour.
  • Includes a secured local tooling host for inspecting every entity set.

Why the boundary matters

A consistent data foundation prevents every domain from inventing its own connection, filtering and persistence conventions.

How it fits

The domain is published and tested independently, then composed through cCoder.Core when an application needs the complete platform. That keeps ownership visible while preserving a straightforward application bootstrap.

Getting started

The source, current README, sample hosts and tests live in cCoder.Data on GitHub. The repository README is the version-specific starting point; the outline below explains how the pieces fit together.

Reference the package

<PackageReference Include="cCoder.Data" Version="YOUR_VERSION" />

During coordinated local development the repositories may substitute a sibling ProjectReference. Published applications should normally consume the agreed package version so the dependency boundary remains explicit.

Register it in the host

builder.Services.AddCoreData(connectionString);

Configure and run it

ConnectionStrings:Core is required. The local Data.Web tooling host also needs the SSO connection and decryption key because the shared context applies user-aware filters.

Consume the capability

Inject CoreDataContext or the domain broker built over it. For inspection and development, run the authenticated Data.Web CRUD host rather than exposing the context as a public application API.

Build and verify from source

git clone https://github.com/ccoder-co-uk/cCoder.Data.git
cd cCoder.Data
dotnet build
dotnet test

Use the repository-specific solution and test commands from its README when working on the domain itself; the standalone and acceptance-test hosts show the supported application boundary more accurately than an isolated snippet can.
